CENTRAL REGISTRY
when finished with it.

Commandant S.V.C.
Shanghai Municipal Council.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE (DETECTIVE BRANCH)）

C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No 31
Date 1-2-16
February 1st 1916.

Sir,
The City Police have received instructions to examine all papers and bills being carried about by people between now and the Chinese new year. It is said that this order has been given because it was reported that the rebels intended to go around distributing seditious literature at new year time, and that they hoped to escape the vigilance of the Authorities by pretending that they were shroffs collecting debts. It is said that the City merchants are very upset on account of the order.

It is reported that a rebel leader named Faung Sung Dau arrived recently from Japan, and that he will make final arrangements for the rising here. Previous to the second revolution, Faung was a military officer in Canton, where he was very popular with his brother officers. Since Faung arrived in Shanghai, he has met four representatives of the Yunnan revolutionists who urged him to start a rising in Shanghai before the new year. Faung told them that he did not expect to be able to do anything so soon, but he hoped to be able to induce the troops here to go over to the rebels quietly.

Four Arsenal detectives were dismissed yesterday for incompetency.

It is reported that the Central Government has decided to separate the offices of Taoyin and Commissioner for Foreign Affairs in Shanghai. The former office will be filled by Mr. Chow and will be situated in Chapei, while the latter office will be taken over by Mr. Yang Tscheng, and will be situated in the Bureau of Foreign Affairs on Bubbling Well Road. It is said that a house belonging to Yu Yah Ching 虞洽卿 which is situated in Zung Tsung Li alleyway off North Chekiang Road, O.O.L. will be occupied by the Taoyin.

The China Mail S.S. Co's S.S. "China" arrived at Woosung yesterday afternoon. In addition to the Company's tender, she was met by the tender "Paula" of the Hamburg American Line, which conveyed a German named Melcher from the ship to the jetty. Melcher is now staying at the Kalee Hotel. It is said that he was a prisoner of war either in Japan or Hongkong.

Captain Superintendent of Police.
McBain Anderson Sgt

中央登记处

上海公共租界工部局警务总监。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处（侦探股））

刑事侦缉处
情报官登记处
第 31 号
日期 1916年2月1日

先生：

华界警方已奉命检查从现在起到中国新年期间人们随身携带的所有文件和票据。据悉，下达此令的原因是有人报告称，反叛分子打算在新年期间四处散发煽动性文献，并希望通过伪装成收账的银房职员来逃避当局的监视。据说，华界商人因这项命令而感到非常不安。

据报，一名名为 Faung Sung Dau（音译）的反叛头目最近从日本抵达，他将在此地为起义做最后安排。在二次革命之前，Faung 是广州的一名军官，在那里他深受同僚军官的欢迎。自从 Faung 抵达上海后，他会见了四名云南革命党代表，他们敦促他在新年前在上海发动起义。Faung 告诉他们，他不指望能这么快就有所行动，但他希望能促使这里的部队悄悄倒向反叛分子。

兵工厂的四名侦探昨日因不称职而被解雇。

据报，中央政府已决定将上海道尹与交涉员的职务分开。前者将由周先生担任，办公地点设在闸北；后者将由杨正先生接管，办公地点设在静安寺路的交涉公署。据说，位于北浙江路（老北区）宗仁里的一处属于虞洽卿的房屋将被道尹占用。

中国邮政轮船公司的“中国”号轮船于昨日下午抵达吴淞。除了该公司的接驳船外，汉堡-美洲航运公司的接驳船“宝拉”号也前来迎接，并将一名名叫 Melcher（音译）的德国人从船上送至码头。Melcher 现住在卡利饭店。据说他曾是日本或香港的战俘。

警察总巡官
麦班·安德森 警长
